$schema-note: Golden characterization corpus for the guard's decision contract, exercised through analyzeCommand() (the in-tree analyzer + guard-level hardening such as the ANSI-C reveal-only probe). Fields: command (string), cwd ('{TMP}' scratch temp dir | '{REPO}' scratch git repo; default {TMP}), expect ('allow'|'ask'|'block') or expectNot, note. For KNOWN analyzer gaps set expectFail:true AND actual:'<current real verdict>' — the runner passes only while the live verdict EQUALS actual, and FAILS the moment it changes in either direction (gap fixed to `expect`, or drifted to a third verdict), forcing this corpus and KNOWN_ANALYZER_GAPS.md to be updated together. Commands may reference {REPO} inside the command string; it resolves to the scratch repo's absolute path. expectOn ({"<process.platform>": "allow|ask|block"}) overrides expect on that platform, for verdicts that are genuinely OS-dependent (e.g. the /Users/* blanket rule has no /home/* Linux equivalent).

KNOWN ANALYZER GAP (fail-open, gap #3 family): the single-quote idiom reassembles the bytes `$'rm'` for the inner shell, which decodes the ANSI-C. Unlike the plain-`rm` control above (which blocks), the analyzer's shell -c recursion does not decode the reassembled ANSI-C, and the guard's probe can't either — the `$'rm'` bytes are non-contiguous in the source (built by outer quote removal), the same dynamic-assembly boundary as eval. Sandbox-backstopped.

The analyzer splits on raw newlines regardless of quoting, so reveal-only cannot distinguish the two uses — it over-blocks the benign echo rather than risk the fail-open. CHARACTERIZATION, platform-split: on macOS the scratch repo lives under /Users/* which the analyzer's blanket catastrophic rule blocks outright (conservative over-blocking, safe direction). On Linux there is no /home/* blanket rule, so the repo-root safe-root logic decides and allows an absolute path under the repo from inside it. Both are the analyzer's real verdicts; a change on either OS should surface here.
